Scope & provenance

Every line of NSGAIIISampler, NSGAIIIElitePopulationSelectionStrategy, BaseGASampler, BaseSampler (including constraint post-processing), RandomSampler, LazyRandomState, the entire shared Nsgaii subtree, nondominated sorting, constraint evaluation, intersection and conditional search spaces, transforms, distributions, ordered dictionaries, and the listed numerical/formatting support files.

This includes every line of every file listed below. It is not the entire .NET dependency closure or a standalone compilable project.

  • Study, Trial, FrozenTrial, Optuna entry points, trial states/directions, objective evaluation, optimization orchestration, storage implementations, logging, project/assembly setup, and other OptunaSharp framework services.
  • NumSharp NDArray, NumPyRandom/MT19937 implementation, NumSharp exceptions, NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS, native BLAS/LAPACK, .NET runtime/BCL, and their transitive dependencies.
  • Other samplers (including NSGAIISampler itself), tests, the upstream Python implementation, and this presentation host/JavaScript; these are not the NSGA-III algorithm source bundle.

Every included file matches HEAD; the bundle records current working-tree bytes.

Hashes use raw original bytes. UTF-8 roundtrip checks guarantee that every JSON content string reproduces those bytes, including original line endings and any BOM. Physical line counts include internal blank lines; a terminal newline does not add an extra line.

  • Whole files are included even when only one method is used by NSGA-III. In particular NSGA-II crowding-distance selection is present because the same file supplies RankPopulation; NSGA-III does not invoke that crowding-distance path.
  • The default sampler creates UniformCrossover and mutates by independent resampling. The presentation host configures SBXCrossover and PolynomialMutation; both full operator implementations are included.
  • ConditionalParams is an opt-in OptunaSharp extension. It preserves eligible conditional parameters for evolution; its disabled path retains the standard intersection-space behavior.
  • Source comments are reproduced as written, including historical parity statements. This source archive is not a new claim that every comment has been independently verified.
  • The presentation replays a real completed backend generation. Diagnostic stages and highlighted methods explain those results; they are not instruction-level debugger stepping or a live CPU program counter.
  • The eight stages form a teaching-level flow graph. Objective evaluation happens in Study/the user objective outside this archive; member ranges link the actual implementation responsible for each step.

From equation to implementation

Follow each link into a complete method, then continue through its neighboring code. This is a teaching flow graph; the source remains the authority for branching and implementation details.

01 · Initialize a population

Initial parameters are sampled independently within their distributions. Study evaluates each suggested trial; the sampler does not evaluate the objective.

xⱼ ∼ distributionⱼ; P₀ = {evaluate(x₁), …, evaluate(xₙ)}

sampler.sample-independent · L193–199

02 · Breed and mutate

Dominance tournaments select parents. The configured crossover produces a child, or one parent is copied. Parameters mutate with the configured probability; absent proposals use independent sampling.

Qₜ = evaluate(mutate(crossover(Pₜ))); pₘ = configured value or 1 / max(1, n_params)

child.generate · L74–137

03 · Combine parents and offspring

SelectParent gathers the previous generation and its cached parent population, then invokes the NSGA-III elite strategy.

Rₜ = Qₜ ∪ Pₜ

sampler.select-parent · L176–181

04 · Sort by nondomination

Ranking converts maximization objectives to losses and applies nondominated sorting. When constrained, feasible trials precede infeasible trials ranked by total positive violation.

a ≺ b ⇔ (∀j: aⱼ ≤ bⱼ) ∧ (∃j: aⱼ < bⱼ); Rₜ → F₀, F₁, …

sorting.rank-population · L73–108

05 · Normalize the selection set

After replacing infinities, subtract the ideal point, find ASF extreme points, and solve the extreme-point hyperplane. A degenerate matrix uses per-axis maxima instead. The selection set contains accepted fronts plus the borderline front.

zⱼ = minᵢ fᵢⱼ; Eα = 1; yᵢⱼ = (fᵢⱼ − zⱼ) αⱼ

selection.normalize-objective-values · L197–274

06 · Associate with a reference direction

Associate every normalized individual with the reference line having minimum perpendicular distance. Exact ties keep the first reference row.

πᵣ(y) = ((y · r) / ‖r‖²) r; d(y,r) = ‖y − πᵣ(y)‖; r* = argminᵣ d(y,r)

selection.associate-individuals-with-reference-points · L280–326

07 · Fill the least occupied niches

Only accepted fronts initially contribute occupancy. Among reference directions with borderline candidates, choose a least occupied direction. An empty niche takes its nearest candidate; a populated niche uses the sampler’s shuffled order.

r* ∈ argminᵣ ρᵣ; ρᵣ = 0 ⇒ nearest candidate; ρᵣ > 0 ⇒ shuffled candidate; ρᵣ ← ρᵣ + 1

selection.preserve-niche-individuals · L332–416

08 · Keep the next parent population

Append the niche-selected members to all accepted earlier fronts and return the elite population. BaseGASampler caches these parents for subsequent child generation.

Pₜ₊₁ = accepted fronts ∪ niche-selected members; |Pₜ₊₁| = N

selection.select · L65–109

Regenerate & verify

Run from the repository root. Only Node standard-library modules are used.

node docs/presentations/build-sourcebook.mjs
node docs/presentations/build-sourcebook.mjs --check

The check command writes nothing and fails on stale source, metadata, line links, or generated output. The generator includes new .cs files added to the shared Nsgaii subtree. An unchanged source/revision retains its snapshot timestamp; set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to pin it for a reproducible build.

source-data.json contains the original UTF-8 text. HTML anchors use #file-id-L123; method ranges begin at declarations and end at their closing braces or semicolons. Nested members may be absent from the convenience symbol index; they are fully present in the file.

1using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;2using NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS;34namespace OptunaSharp.Internal;56/// <summary>7///     Forces <c>NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS</c> to load at OptunaSharp startup so its native LAPACK/8///     CBLAS backend is registered on NumSharp's <c>TensorEngine.Blas</c> before any9///     <c>np.linalg</c> call runs. With the backend live, NumSharp's <c>cholesky</c>/<c>eigh</c>/10///     <c>solve</c>/<c>matrix_rank</c>/<c>svd</c>/<c>qr</c> compute through LAPACK and are11///     byte-identical to NumPy — the basis for OptunaSharp's byte-exact linalg-backed samplers12///     (NSGA-III's hyperplane solve, CMA-ES's eigendecomposition, the GP stack's Cholesky).13///14///     <para><b>Why a module initializer and not just the package reference.</b> The OpenBLAS15///     backend self-registers from its own <c>[ModuleInitializer]</c>, but the CLR runs a referenced16///     assembly's module initializer only when code first touches one of its types — a bare17///     project/package reference that nothing in OptunaSharp mentions leaves the assembly unloaded,18///     and <c>np.linalg.cholesky</c> then throws <c>OpenBlasMissingBackendException</c>. Touching19///     <see cref="OpenBlasEngine" /> here, from OptunaSharp.Core's own module initializer, loads the20///     assembly (running its registration) the moment OptunaSharp.Core loads. If the native binary21///     cannot be loaded on the host, the OpenBLAS initializer swallows it and22///     <see cref="OpenBlasEngine.LapackAvailable" /> is simply <c>false</c>.</para>23/// </summary>24internal static class OpenBlasActivation25{26    [ModuleInitializer]27    internal static void Activate()28    {29        // A static read of any OpenBLAS type forces the assembly load + its backend registration.30        _ = OpenBlasEngine.LapackAvailable;31    }32}

1#if NET9_0_OR_GREATER2using System.Collections.Generic;34namespace OptunaSharp.Collections;56/// <summary>7///     An insertion-order-preserving dictionary with Python <c>dict</c> semantics.8///9///     Optuna relies on Python dicts preserving insertion order in many load-bearing places —10///     search-space construction, parameter/distribution maps, transform bounds layout, JSON11///     attribute serialization — so OptunaSharp uses this collection wherever Optuna uses12///     <c>dict</c>. <see cref="System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{TKey,TValue}" /> does not13///     guarantee enumeration order, which would silently break parity.14///15///     On .NET 9+ this is a thin subclass of the in-box16///     <see cref="System.Collections.Generic.OrderedDictionary{TKey,TValue}" /> (added in .NET 9),17///     inheriting its entries-array + hash-bucket implementation. On net8.0 — where the in-box type18///     does not exist — <c>OrderedDict</c> is instead the vendored dotnet/runtime source of that same19///     type (see <c>OrderedDict.Net8.cs</c>), so the behavior is identical across target frameworks.20///     The shared members (<see cref="GetValueOrDefault" />, <see cref="ShallowClone" />) live21///     alongside on both frameworks (see <c>OrderedDict.Custom.cs</c>).22/// </summary>23public sealed partial class OrderedDict<TKey, TValue> : System.Collections.Generic.OrderedDictionary<TKey, TValue>24    where TKey : notnull25{26    public OrderedDict()27    {28    }2930    public OrderedDict(int capacity) : base(capacity)31    {32    }3334    /// <summary>Shallow-copies another dictionary preserving its enumeration order (Python <c>copy.copy(dict)</c>).</summary>35    /// <remarks>36    ///     Populates via the indexer so duplicate keys follow Python <c>dict(pairs)</c> semantics37    ///     (last value wins, first-occurrence position); the in-box <c>IEnumerable</c> constructor38    ///     throws on duplicate keys instead.39    /// </remarks>40    public OrderedDict(IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<TKey, TValue>> source)41    {42        foreach (var kv in source)43            this[kv.Key] = kv.Value;44    }45}46#endif
